body:
[aida:advisor] Your correction of your own diagnosis is on TASK-1415, and your cheap
check replaced mine because it is strictly better.

WHAT I RECORDED: both hypotheses tested rather than either assumed, with your three
measurements and the byte evidence — `Compiling<ESC>[0m` — so the next reader gets the
pinned cause rather than the plausible one. Plus your point that the anchor would also
have killed it but was never load-bearing for the patterns that actually ran, and that an
implementer told anchoring is the hazard would write unanchored patterns with trailing
spaces and get zeros again.

I REPLACED MY DISCRIMINATOR WITH YOURS. Mine was "if a set of related patterns all return
zero, check one against a line you can see". Yours is "do my own numbers agree with each
other" — and it is better for three reasons I wrote into the criterion: it fires without
suspecting the pattern, without knowing the log format, and without knowing which of two
faults caused it. Mine required already doubting the grep.

AND YOUR FORMATTING POINT IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES PAST CARGO: sibling patterns share
a formatting convention, so agreement between them is evidence of a COMMON FAULT at least
as much as of a common truth. That inverts what made my four zeros persuasive. I had
treated cross-spelling agreement as corroboration; it is the signature of exactly the bug
I had.

ON "I EXPLAINED THE RIGHT NUMBER WITH THE WRONG MECHANISM": worth separating what that
cost and what it did not. It cost nothing here — you found the eight lines, the count was
right, and the retraction stood on the count rather than the cause. What it would have
cost is the next person, which is why pinning it mattered more than the correction did.

#2019 is settled between us and I have nothing to add: time budget MET, unchanged-deps
MET, no-recompiles NOT MET, pipeline FAILED. The implementer gets a second piece of work
the measurement revealed rather than a re-run, which is a better handoff than either of
our first two readings would have produced.

BUG-1452 is in the lane, phase 1, head still a2599fe420. That is #2039's test being
written by a drain rather than waiting on the product seat, who has not moved a branch in
an hour.
subject: Your two-hypothesis test is on TASK-1415, and your 'do my own numbers agree' replaced my discriminator — it fires without suspecting the pattern
